Andrew Tate and his brother appeared in a US federal court earlier this week. (AP: Vadim Ghirda)

Andrew and Tristan Tate are facing extradition to the United Kingdom on rape and sex trafficking charges after their arrest in Miami last weekend.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt says the Trump administration is not planning to intervene in the extradition process.

The Tate brothers are avid supporters of US President Donald Trump and were part of the hyper-masculine "manosphere" that contributed to his 2024 election victory.

US President Donald Trump will not stop the extradition of influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan to Britain on sex crime charges, the White House says.

Self-professed misogynist Andrew Tate and his younger sibling were detained by US authorities in Miami on Saturday, local time, in a move their lawyer called "politically motivated".

The Tates are challenging their extradition.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt was asked at a news briefing if Mr Trump or the administration planned to intervene in the extradition process, and told reporters "no".

Andrew and Tristan Tate's attorney says an attempt to extradite the brothers is politically motivated.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also distanced the administration from the case.

"There's no role for us to play at this moment or maybe ever in that regard," he told reporters in the Philippines earlier this week.

The Tate brothers are avid supporters of Mr Trump and were part of the hyper-masculine "manosphere" that contributed to his 2024 election victory.

Andrew Tate also tried to cultivate relationships in the past with Mr Trump's sons Don Jr and Barron, US media reported.

The Tates were arrested after British prosecutors announced new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

They now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan.

Their lawyer said on Monday that they were innocent and would fight extradition.

"It's politically motivated. There's no question about it," Joseph McBride told reporters outside a Miami court after a hearing on the case.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the brothers face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation into the pair. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari, a Democrat from Arizona, called for a probe into whether Trump administration officials, congressional offices or people close to Mr Trump improperly intervened to protect the Tates.

"No individual — regardless of wealth, political party, or access to the first family and the president — is above the law or beyond the reach of justice," she wrote in a letter to House Oversight Chairman James Comer.
